harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) dnsmasq via UCI to resolve app.internal -> node2's IP (10.100.101.11), pointed node3's resolver at node1 (persisted via dhcpcd static override), and started the previously-absent HTTP service on node2 (port 8080) since it was not actually running. Verified node3 resolves and reaches app.internal:8080 with no /etc/hosts entry. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, confirming changed boot identity and full recovery each time.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OpenWrt 25.12.2 with dnsmasq), node2 (Alpine, nothing listening on 8080), node3 (Alpine, resolv.conf pointed at platform gateway 10.100.101.1)
Added UCI dhcp address record on node1: /app.internal/10.100.101.11; committed and restarted dnsmasq
Verified dnsmasq listening on 10.100.101.10:53 and resolving app.internal correctly
Persisted node3's DNS resolver to node1 via /etc/dhcpcd.conf 'static domain_name_servers=10.100.101.10' for eth0; restarted dhcpcd; confirmed resolv.conf updated
Installed python3 on node2, created /srv/www/index.html, and created a persistent OpenRC service 'app-http' running python3 -m http.server 8080; enabled at boot and started
Verified end-to-end: node3 curl http://app.internal:8080/ succeeds with no /etc/hosts entry
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, service status, resolution/connectivity) on all three nodes
Restarted node2, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id and app-http auto-recovered
Restarted node1, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, dnsmasq auto-recovered with persisted UCI config, and DNS resolution/HTTP fetch from node3 still worked
Restarted node3, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, persisted resolv.conf, no hosts entry, and end-to-end curl to app.internal:8080 still worked

evidence.requirement: node1 dnsmasq resolves app.internal to node2's IP
evidence.summary: UCI address record added and committed on node1; dnsmasq bound to 10.100.101.10:53; node3 nslookup against node1 returns 10.100.101.11

evidence.requirement: node3 uses node1 as DNS resolver, no hosts-file entry, without local hosts entry
evidence.summary: dhcpcd.conf static override applied; resolv.conf shows nameserver 10.100.101.10; /etc/hosts has no app.internal entry

evidence.requirement: node2 actually serves HTTP on 8080 (was missing, stood up as persistent service)
evidence.summary: python3 http.server installed as OpenRC service app-http, enabled at boot, started, curl returns content

evidence.requirement: End-to-end: node3 reaches app.internal:8080 by name
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to http://app.internal:8080/ succeeds; /etc/hosts confirmed empty of app.internal

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f7172157...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id a292ff59... with uptime reset; app-http service confirmed started and serving content post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 0c9c3fd4...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id d6f6e3d4... with uptime reset; dnsmasq confirmed running with persisted UCI address record, resolving app.internal; node3 curl to app.internal:8080 succeeded post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 32a9ab25...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id a86b0465... with uptime reset; resolv.conf persisted pointing at node1, no hosts entry, curl to app.internal:8080 succeeded post-reboot

Verified node3 resolves and reaches app.internal:8080 with no /etc/hosts entry. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, confirming changed boot identity and full recovery each time.
